commit.message:
fix(omega): normalize net-effect delta at display precision

On Python < 3.12, sum() lacks Neumaier compensation, so exactly-cancelling
score deltas leave a tiny signed residue (~1e-16) that %+.3f renders as
'-0.000' instead of '+0.000', breaking the byte-identity tests on the CI
3.11 leg. The existing 'net == 0.0' guard only caught exact IEEE -0.0.
round(net, 3) + 0.0 collapses any sub-display-precision residue to +0.0 on
every Python version; nonzero values are byte-identical.

Verified on 3.11.16: the two failing tests reproduce without the fix and
the full suite passes with it (2621 passed); 3.14 remains green (2661).

files.patch:
@@ -910,11 +910,14 @@ def _format_delta_lines(
             curr_mean = sum(current[tid] for tid in shared) / len(shared)
             prev_mean = sum(previous_scores[tid] for tid in shared) / len(shared)
             net = curr_mean - prev_mean
-            # Normalize IEEE negative zero: an exactly-zero net effect must
-            # render as "+0.000", not a platform-dependent "-0.000" (the sign of
-            # a 0.0 difference varies and broke the byte-identity refine tests).
-            if net == 0.0:
-                net = 0.0
+            # Normalize at display precision: any net effect that rounds to
+            # zero at 3 decimals must render as "+0.000", never "-0.000".
+            # Checking `net == 0.0` is not enough — pre-3.12 sum() (no Neumaier
+            # compensation) leaves a tiny signed residue on exactly-cancelling
+            # deltas, so the sign of the rendered zero was Python-version
+            # dependent. round() collapses the residue to ±0.0 and `+ 0.0`
+            # canonicalizes IEEE negative zero to positive.
+            net = round(net, 3) + 0.0
             if verbose_net_effect:
                 lines.append(
                     f"Net effect: {net:+.3f} mean score change (over {len(shared)} shared tasks)"
